title: Ellipsoid–hyperboloid intersection conjecture
statement:
Let $M$ be a real positive matrix, let $\mathbf{1}=(1,\dots,1)$, and let $\mathcal{E}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:x^\top Mx=n\}$ be the associated ellipsoid. Let $\mathcal{H}$ denote the hyperboloid used in the source.

**Ellipsoid–hyperboloid conjecture.** If the diagonal of $M$ is $\lambda\mathbf{1}$ and the ellipsoid $\mathcal{E}$ meets every branch of $\mathcal{H}$, then $\lambda\leqslant1$.

This is presented as a scaled geometric reformulation of the inverse-eigenvector conjecture. The source does not give a proof or disproof.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.05379

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).
source_name: Gergely Ambrus, “Analytic and Probabilistic Problems in Discrete Geometry”, arXiv:1907.05379 (2019).
